newsitem.title: UK: Oil slips as market braces for Iraqi return.
newsitem.headline: Oil slips as market braces for Iraqi return.

text.p: World oil prices eased on Wednesday as bearish sentiment induced by the renewal of Iraqi exports and the sale of German strategic oil reserves dampened the impact of a buoyant U.S. gasoline market.
While crude and refined product markets often move in tandem, a robust summer rally in gasoline prices has failed to inspire a similar move on crude markets.
Crude has found itself hemmed in by strong resistance levels - a series of price ceilings above which traders are reluctant to buy without a change in supply and demand fundamentals.
"Gasoline has moved into higher ground, but crude has run into strong resistance...We are seeing a two-tier market emerging," said Christopher Bellew of Prudential Bache Futures in London.
International benchmark Brent crude futures for September were trading eight cents lower at $18.77 a barrel at 1652 GMT.
In contrast, gasoline futures had gained nearly one cent a gallon in New York.
Figures released by the U.S. Department of Energy on Wednesday showed that gasoline stock levels were falling in an already tight market.

Gasoline inventories in the world's largest oil market fell 1.5 million barrels last week, while stocks of low emission reformulated gasoline, the grade quoted in the futures market, fell a hefty 2.7 million barrels.
But traders were keeping a close eye on Iraqi developments, with the first tanker of Iraqi crude since late May expected to load later on Wednesday at the Turkish port of Ceyhan.
The Arcadia, a giant, two-million-barrel tanker chartered by U.S. trading company Bayoil, was scheduled to load at around midnight local time, or 2000 GMT.
"It seems the main reason that crude is not following gasoline is because of Iraqi sales...and ultimately it's going to separate the markets more," said Bellew.
Exports under the United Nations "oil-for-food" deal with Iraq have been stalled for nearly three months due to wrangling over an aid distribution plan.

Iraq has scheduled exports of 1.45 million barrels per day (bpd) for the remainder of August as it races to raise as much cash as possible by an interim deadline of September 5 for $1 billion worth of sales.
Adding to supply pressures are sales of crude from German strategic stocks to plug holes in government finances and help meet the criteria for European economic and monetary union.

The first tranche, some 2.8 million barrels of sour crudes, were sold to four oil companies in a tender on Tuesday. The oil is expected to stay in Europe for refining in Germany, Sweden and the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region.
